title: Employer UI Tax Accounts: Wage Share Schedule by Days of Report Lateness
content:
On the Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts, the percentage of total wages used in the late report penalty's comparison with the flat penalty follows the report's lateness. A report's lateness is the number of calendar days from its due date to its filing date, measured on the original report the penalty is worked out from — the original report with the latest filing date on the account.

| Lateness of the report | Percentage of total wages used |
|---|---|
| More than 90 days | 0.003 (0.3%) |
| More than 30 days, but no more than 90 days | 0.002 (0.2%) |
| No more than 30 days | The class's late report percentage |

## Both sides of each boundary (hypothetical report due on 30 April)

| Filed on | Days late | Percentage used |
|---|---|---|
| 30 May | 30 | The class's late report percentage |
| 31 May | 31 | 0.002 |
| 29 July | 90 | 0.002 |
| 30 July | 91 | 0.003 |

**Illustration (hypothetical).** A report showing total wages of USD 180,000.00 and filed 45 days late uses 0.002, which gives USD 360.00 for the comparison with the flat penalty; filed 120 days late it uses 0.003, which gives USD 540.00.
